chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who visits his brother while he is fasting, and breaks his fast in his presence, and does not inform him of his fasting so as to do him a favour, Allah will write for him the fasting of a year.'

key_terms.فَيَمُنَّ عَلَيْهِ: So he does him a favour / shows generosity

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for breaking the fast of a fasting person who does not know they are fasting?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the high spiritual status of *aman* (generosity) in breaking a fasting person's fast, particularly when the host does not explicitly invite them but provides food. This act is rewarded with the equivalent of fasting for a year, emphasizing the social etiquette of sharing sustenance and the merit of removing the burden of fasting from a brother in faith. The tradition underscores the importance of subtle generosity and the communal aspect of worship in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said,

‘Abu Abullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who goes over to his brother and he is Fasting, so he breaks in his presence and he does not let him know of his Fast that he is doing him a favour, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Fasts of a year’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If a fasting person visits his brother (in belief) who offers him food, and he accepts the offer without telling him about his fast, in order not to show that he is doing him a favor, Allah counts his fast as one year’s fasting.’”
